_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla, typed out on the slip. Each lesson has two: "start" comes on as the lesson opens, and "check" is a short quiz once the lesson's check is done. Each talk has turns; in each turn Walla Walla says "them" and the player picks one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."). A reply can have a "back" line, and "right": true marks the right answer to a question (it is never scored). Every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. August, and the afternoons are hot. This week’s question is the one that keeps threshing crews safe: will those puffy clouds blow up into a thunderstorm, and when do you get everybody indoors?

replies.back: Don’t sound so pleased. A storm doesn’t care how much you’ve studied.

turns.them: How a heap becomes a storm, how to feel one coming, and how to count the distance to its lightning. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. When does a thunderstorm throw its lightning and downpours?

replies.say: The mature stage, once the downdraught starts.
replies.back: Updraught and downdraught side by side. That’s when you want everybody under a roof.
Not yet. Growing, it’s all updraught. The trouble starts when rain and hail drag a downdraught down with them: the mature stage.
By then it’s raining itself out. The worst is the mature stage.

turns.them: Flash! Then thunder, nine seconds later. How far off?

replies.back: Nine divided by three. And that’s under thirty seconds, so everyone indoors.
Divide by three: about three kilometres. Under thirty seconds, so everyone indoors.
Three kilometres is close enough to be struck. Under thirty seconds, get indoors.

turns.them: A hot afternoon, and a sudden cool, gusty wind comes out from under a dark tower. What’s coming?

replies.back: Right. That’s the gust front, running out ahead of the storm.
Not yet. A cool gust under a tower is the gust front, minutes ahead of the downpour.
It’s the storm’s own cold air spilling out ahead of it. The downpour is 5 to 15 minutes behind.

turns.them: And thirty minutes after the last thunder before anybody goes back out. Two lessons left, for autumn and winter.
